The increase is mainly attributable to higher uptake and fuller pass-through of Dext costs to clients, with larger recharges to a small number of higher-usage clients and fewer discounts or under-recoveries compared with the prior year.

Fee Protection Costs (4100-2) – £12,038.14 vs £7,409.42 – £4,628.72 increase (62%): current year costs of £12,038.14 primarily comprise increased fee protection cover charges and related service fees recharged to clients, with the main movements being higher annual premiums and a greater volume of client take‑up compared with last year, but last year the £7,409.42 balance reflected a lower level of cover and fewer participating clients. The increase is mainly attributable to higher charges from the firm’s fee protection provider and associated intermediaries (for example, increased policy and service costs from the main insurance/broker counterparties) because of expanded cover limits, price rises in the market, and a higher number of client policies written in the year compared with the prior period.

Fee protection income (4100-1) – £71,421.15 vs £46,718.32 – £24,702.83 increase (53%): current year income of £71,421.15 comprises ongoing annual fee protection charges to clients on recurring service packages together with a noticeable uplift in new sign‑ups and upgrades during the year, whereas last year’s £46,718.32 reflected a smaller fee protection client base and fewer new policies taken out. The increase is mainly driven by higher volumes of clients opting into fee protection as part of their annual renewal cycle and mid‑year take‑up from existing clients upgrading their service level, with the most significant contributions arising from a small number of larger client groups moving onto bundled compliance and protection packages, because of a targeted push on fee protection at renewal, increased HMRC enquiry activity communicated to clients, and a full‑year impact of policies sold late in the prior year now renewing at higher rates in the current year.

Entertaining – Staff (7404) – £871.64 vs £601.53 – £270.11 increase (45%): this year’s £871.64 mainly comprises staff meals and drinks for team events and ad‑hoc staff lunches, including larger one‑off staff social gatherings and increased frequency of smaller team lunches, but last year, the £601.53 was largely limited to occasional staff lunches and a smaller year‑end gathering with fewer attendees and lower spend per head. The increase is primarily due to a conscious decision to hold more regular staff social events and team‑building activities during the year, with higher average spend per event and greater staff participation compared with the prior year.

ERS NIC (6001) – £79,885.31 vs £87,418.47 – £7,533.16 decrease (9%): the current year charge of £79,885.31 reflects employer’s NIC on the increased payroll but with a lower effective rate due to higher utilisation of allowances and changes in staff mix, whereas last year’s £87,418.47 included higher ERS NIC on several senior roles and bonuses that have not recurred at the same level.
